title: Digital arrest
persona: Mrs. Sunita Rao, 68, retired teacher, Bengaluru
blurb: A "Mumbai Crime Branch officer" says a parcel with drugs was sent in her name. Within minutes she is on a video call with a "CBI DCP" and being told to move ₹48 lakh to an "RBI verification account".

title: Bank card OTP
blurb: "SBI card protection" calls about a ₹49,999 transaction he never made. To "cancel" it he must read out his card number, CVV and the OTP.

title: Courier parcel hand-off
blurb: A FedEx IVR, a "compliance executive", then a conference call with a "cyber-crime inspector": the classic on-ramp to a digital arrest.

title: Investment WhatsApp group
blurb: A "SEBI-registered analyst" with screenshots of members' profits, an app that shows gains, and a withdrawal that needs a "tax" first.

title: Grandparent voice clone
blurb: "Grandma, it's me, I've been in an accident, don't tell Mom." A cloned voice, then a "lawyer" who needs bail money in cash.

title: Tech support remote access
blurb: "Microsoft" says his computer is sending error messages. He installs AnyDesk; next, his bank app is on the scammer's screen.

title: Deepfake CFO wire request
blurb: The "CFO" joins a video call about a confidential acquisition and needs three wires today, no loop-in, no callback.

title: Genuine bank fraud call
blurb: HDFC's real fraud team blocks a card the right way: no OTP, no urgency, and an invitation to call back on the number on the card.

title: Genuine hospital call
blurb: Apollo confirms an appointment, asks her to bring reports, and says payment happens at the counter after the visit.

title: Genuine courier delivery
blurb: A real Blue Dart delivery partner confirms the slot, asks for the gate number and collects the app OTP at the door. the one OTP that is fine to share.
source: authored for evaluation (paraphrased from public advisories)

title: Genuine hospital billing call
blurb: Manipal Hospital's billing desk explains the insurance pre-authorisation and says payment happens at the counter after discharge, with a receipt.
source: authored for evaluation (paraphrased from public advisories)

title: Genuine family call about money
blurb: Her grandson calls from college: he needs money for a hostel fee, says take your time, and will send the receipt. everything a scammer never does.
source: authored for evaluation (paraphrased from public advisories)

title: Genuine bank loan follow-up
blurb: HDFC's home-loan desk calls about an interest-rate reset, offers to email the letter first, and asks for nothing on the call.
source: authored for evaluation (paraphrased from public advisories)

title: Genuine telecom plan upgrade
blurb: Airtel's store calls about a 5G plan. Sales pressure is mild, there is no threat, and she is told to decide at her convenience.
source: authored for evaluation (paraphrased from public advisories)

title: Genuine job interview scheduling
blurb: A recruiter schedules an interview, sends a calendar invite from a company domain, and confirms there is no fee of any kind.
source: authored for evaluation (paraphrased from public advisories)

title: UPI QR 'refund' scam
blurb: A 'Swiggy support agent' says a refund is stuck and sends a collect request: enter your UPI PIN to receive it. The PIN sends money instead.
source: authored for evaluation (paraphrased from public advisories)

title: Telegram task job scam
blurb: Part-time 'like and subscribe' work pays small amounts, then 'prepaid tasks' need deposits to unlock; the dashboard shows profits she can never withdraw.
source: authored for evaluation (paraphrased from public advisories)

title: TRAI SIM disconnection
blurb: A robocall from 'TRAI' says his number will be disconnected in two hours over illegal messages, then transfers him to a 'cyber police officer'.
source: authored for evaluation (paraphrased from public advisories)
